figures.alt: Circuit schematic labeled Figure T-1 showing a small circuit with five individually numbered component call-outs and two ground symbols.
Circuit schematic labeled Figure T-2 with ten individually numbered component call-outs connecting a source on the left to an output terminal on the right, plus several ground symbols.
Circuit schematic labeled Figure T-3 showing a small matching network with four individually numbered component call-outs and a ground symbol.
Circuit schematic labeled Figure G7-1 with eleven individually numbered component call-outs, a positive supply rail marked plus DC, and an output terminal marked OUT.
Graph labeled Figure E5-1: a rectangular X and Y coordinate grid running from -600 to 600 on each axis, with eight small plotted dots labeled Point 1 through Point 8.
Figure E6-1: six numbered semiconductor schematic symbols, each drawn inside a circle with terminal leads marked G, D, and S (symbols 4 and 5 also marked G1 and G2).
Figure E6-2: eight numbered two- and three-terminal semiconductor schematic symbols built on the diode triangle-and-bar shape.
Figure E6-3: six numbered digital logic gate schematic symbols, each with input lines entering from the left and one output line leaving to the right.
Figure E7-1: schematic of a single-transistor circuit with an input marked IN, an output marked OUT, a positive supply rail, resistors R1 to R3, capacitors C1 to C3, and grounds.

Figure E7-2: schematic of a circuit with a 25-volt input on the left and a 12-volt output on the right, containing transistor Q1, semiconductor D1, resistors R1 and R2, capacitors C1 to C3, and grounds.
Figure E7-3: schematic of an operational amplifier with input resistor R1, feedback resistor R-F, an inverting and a noninverting input, an output, and grounds.
Figure E9-1: a full polar antenna radiation pattern plot titled Free-Space Pattern, with azimuth graduations every 30 degrees and concentric rings marked -3, -6, -12, and -24 decibels.
Figure E9-2: a half-polar antenna radiation pattern plot titled Over Real Ground, with angular graduations from 0 to 180 degrees and a radial decibel scale reaching -40.
